samples.summary: Toolbar "Clear formatting" (collapsed caret) still extends a hyperlink — the delta only fixed the Cmd+\ path
samples.evidence: `clearFormatting()` in text-editor.ts:3439-3448 was patched so a collapsed caret at a link's trailing edge re-arms `href: undefined`. The toolbar/API sibling was not. `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` (editor.ts:3344-3350) calls `applyStyleImpl(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)`, and the collapsed branch of `applyStyleImpl` does `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)` (editor.ts:1168-1174). `getSelectionStyleImpl()` → `caretInlineStyle(doc, cursor.position)` returns the raw run style *including* `href` (model/caret-style.ts:71-78), and `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` no longer carries an `href` key (model/types.ts:300) so it cannot override it. Result: with the caret at the trailing edge of a link (e.g. right after `insertLink`, where `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` had armed `href: undefined`), clicking Clear formatting overwrites pending with `href: '<url>'`, and the next typed character is written *into* the link — silently extending it. Before this PR the `href: undefined` inside `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` masked this. Same hazard, same caret, different entry point; the doc comment at text-editor.ts:3418 claims the button and shortcut behave identically, which is no longer true for a collapsed caret.

samples.summary: `prev.href === undefined` re-arms a link exit without checking the pending anchor still matches the caret
samples.evidence: `PendingStyle.get()` (view/pending-style.ts:20) returns only the style, not the anchor, so the new `!!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)` test cannot tell whether the stale `href: undefined` was armed at *this* caret. Because `pending.set(..., this.cursor.position)` re-anchors, a pending state that was previously harmless (it would have been discarded by `consumeForInsert`'s anchor-mismatch branch, pending-style.ts:30-33) becomes live at the new caret and can strip the href off text typed *inside* a link. Most navigation paths call `pending?.clear()`, so I could not pin a concrete reachable sequence — hence low confidence — but the guard is anchor-blind by construction.

samples.summary: Remove-link button silently no-ops when the editor does not implement the optional `removeLink`
samples.evidence: `removeLink?(): void` is optional on `TextFormattingEditor` (types.ts:104), and the handler calls `editor.removeLink?.()`. The button's `disabled` state is `disabled || !editor` only, so a surface that opts into `showRemoveLink` with an editor lacking `removeLink` renders an enabled control that does nothing and gives no feedback. Today both slides call sites supply it, so the reach is contained, but the enable condition and the capability check are not the same predicate.
